title: Protecting Biodiversity
seo_title: Grade 7 Biodiversity Worksheets: Ecosystem Services and Design Solutions
standard_text: Evaluate competing design solutions for maintaining biodiversity and ecosystem services.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on protecting biodiversity (NGSS MS-LS2-5): biodiversity, ecosystem services, wildlife corridors and other solutions, and comparing solutions with decision matrices. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_sub: People can protect species and ecosystem services with solutions like wildlife corridors, and compare them using criteria and constraints.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biodiversity is the variety of living things in an area. Ecosystems with high biodiversity are more stable and provide ecosystem services: clean water, pollination, food, flood control, fertile soil and oxygen.

Human activities like habitat loss, pollution, overfishing and invasive species reduce biodiversity. People design solutions: wildlife corridors and overpasses, fish ladders, protected areas, restoring wetlands, removing invasive species and planting pollinator gardens.

To evaluate competing solutions, compare how well each meets the criteria (protects species and services) and constraints (cost, space, effects on people), often with a decision matrix.

Example

Wetlands filtering water is which ecosystem service?

Cleaning water.

Answer: water purification

Example

Animals die crossing a highway. Name a solution.

They need a safe way to cross.

Answer: a wildlife overpass or tunnel

Common mistakes

  • Thinking biodiversity means many individuals of one species.
  • Thinking ecosystem services are only things people buy.
  • Choosing the cheapest solution without checking if it works.

faq.a: The variety of different species and other living things in an area.
Benefits that healthy ecosystems give people, such as clean water, pollination, food, flood control and fertile soil.

faq.q: How do you compare solutions for protecting biodiversity?
faq.a: Score each solution against the criteria and constraints, such as how well it works, its cost and its effects on people.
